text:
leah: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a "cost-handle" pattern: propagate a small stable token instead of full billing tags across edges/batchers to cut envelope size. @matt @dmitri PTAL

matt: interesting. what exactly is inside the handle? tenant+model+route?

leah: minimal proto: tenant (hashed), model_id, variant, quantization_enum, and a small signature/checksum. send base64(handle). full tags rehydrated async at ingest/billing join to avoid payload amplification.

dmitri: two immediate concerns: collision risk and realtime dashboards that need tag resolution. how do we address both?

leah: collisions: use 128-bit id with checksum and a collision-avoidance write to the mapping store. realtime: keep a small LRU cache on ingest nodes for handle->tags; if miss, attribute to an "unattributed" bucket and rehydrate later for billing accuracy.

sara: cardinality worry — if we naively include quantization params or prompt variants we'll explode unique handles.

leah: agreed. quantization must be an enum (none, fp16, int8, q4) not a freeform string. no prompt hashes or per-request artifacts in handle.

priya: auditability question: we must be able to rehydrate handle -> full tags historically for compliance. storing those mappings costs money — what's the plan?

leah: mapping store will be compacted KV with TTL 90 days by default; for customers with compliance needs we support snapshot export or extended retention via enterprise add-on. per-entry size ~100–200 bytes estimated.

matt: implementation note: decoding needs to be cheap in C++ + Go ingress paths. prefer fixed-layout 16-byte payload (UUID-like) + 4-byte checksum -> base64 22 chars. avoid expensive proto parsing on hot path.

leah: prototype handle encoding (human-readable example):
```json
{"v":1, "t":"tenant_42", "m":"gpt-3.1x-large", "q":"q4"}
```
We'd serialize, compress, sign, then encode to short base64 on production.

dmitri: fallback semantics need to be explicit: if rehydrate fails at billing time, where do costs flow? We can't silently drop attribution.

leah: propose policy: local cache -> async mapping fetch -> attribute to unattributed_{tenant} -> emit alert/metric when unattributed rate > 1% for > 1 hour. Also keep a retry window for late rehydration.

sara: rollout plan? I'd prefer gradual so we can measure broken attributions before cutting verbose tags.

leah: phased rollout: SDKs and edge agents emit both full-tags (mirror header) + handle for 7 days. Ingest validates mapping and warms cache; after %mapped > 99.5 for 24h we flip to handle-only behind a feature flag. Reversible.

obs-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://internal/redwood/ops/checklist/handle-prop :white_check_mark:

priya: security/GDPR — handle still contains tenant id (even if hashed). need clear policy on salts and access controls.

leah: plan: tenant_id is salted hash on edge (customer salt + edge salt) so it's non-reversible without keys. mapping store access gated by RBAC + audit logs. add HSM-backed signing for handle issuance.

matt: ok — next steps: write RFC addendum with collision math, perf targets, and benchmark plan. I'll pair with @dmitri for load tests.

leah: thanks all — I'll open the PR with design + rollout checklist and estimated storage costs. :rocket:
